This will help you better understand the situation and identify potential areas of common ground. 2. **Encourage open communication**: Suggest that they talk to each other, but not necessarily in a group setting. This can help them communicate their feelings and concerns without feeling overwhelmed or defensive. 3. **Focus on the community gathering**: Emphasize the importance of the community gathering and how their presence would benefit everyone. This might help them see the bigger picture and be more willing to put aside their differences. 4. **Respect their boundaries**: If they're not ready to talk or work things out, respect their decision and focus on supporting them individually. Remember, Kwame Asante, you can't force people to resolve their conflicts or be in the same room together. Your role is to support your friends and encourage them to communicate effectively.
